source.author: stat
source.text: caeruleae dux ille comae, quo protinus omnis horruit audito tellus pontusque polusque, et pater Aetnaeos iterum respexit ad ignes, accipit illa sonum; stabat tunc forte parenti proxima, dum coetu Capaneus laudatur ab omni Ditis et insignem Stygiis fovet amnibus umbram, protinus abrupta terrarum mole sub astris constitit, exsultant manes, quantumque profundae rarescunt tenebrae, tantum de luce recessit, excipit atra soror dextraeque innexa profatur:
source.text_original: caeruleae dux ille comae, quo protinus omnis / horruit audito tellus pontusque polusque, / et pater Aetnaeos iterum respexit ad ignes, / accipit illa sonum; stabat tunc forte parenti / proxima, dum coetu Capaneus laudatur ab omni / Ditis et insignem Stygiis fovet amnibus umbram, / protinus abrupta terrarum mole sub astris / constitit, exsultant manes, quantumque profundae / rarescunt tenebrae, tantum de luce recessit, / excipit atra soror dextraeque innexa profatur: /
source.text_english: That leader of blue hair, at whose name all the earth, sea, and sky at once shuddered, and the father looked back again to the fires of Aetna, she hears that sound. She was then by chance standing close beside her father, while Capaneus is being praised by the whole company and the shades celebrate the distinguished shade by the Stygian streams; at once, beneath the stars, the mass of earth suddenly split open and came to a halt, the spirits exult, and just as the deep darkness grows thinner, so much has she withdrawn from the light. The dark sister receives her and, linked by the right hand, speaks:

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: quotiens raucos ad litoris ictus deficiam Scythicum metuens pontumque polumque nec de te credam nostris ingrata serenis.
reuse.text_original: quotiens raucos ad litoris ictus / deficiam Scythicum metuens pontumque polumque / nec de te credam nostris ingrata serenis.
reuse.text_english: How often shall I faint at the hoarse beatings of the shore, fearing the Scythian sea and the sky alike, and in our fair weather shall I not believe a thing about you, ungrateful one?
